items.title: Harry Shields Interview, 1961-05-28
items.q: when I first started playing with Emmet Hardy

ctx.x: Like A, B or B flat?

E flat, B flat, F and for quite a while I would say, which really was my G, I'd call it F, which was my F, I'd call it E flat because I thought Ed was right. So when I first started playing with Emmet Hardy, he knew the difference. So he'd say F, no, E flat for you, but it's really F, but you know it as E flat. So we'd play the tune, I'd play the harmony to him, you know, whatever he'd play.
I was going to ask, in regard to this arranging, head arranging or whatever you want to call it, when you think those things in your head, did you ever study any harmony or any theory?
